title: Explicit null-homotopy for a non-Boolean proper product interval
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $r\geq1$, let $m\in\mathbf N^r$, and choose $j$ with $m_j\geq2$. Give $T=\prod_{i=1}^r\{0,\ldots,m_i\}\setminus\{0,m\}$ its coordinatewise order, and use the augmented strict-chain complex $C(T;R)$ of [def-sfb-augmented-poset-chains]. Put $e_j=1$, $e_i=0$ for $i\ne j$, and put $u(x)_j=\max(x_j,1)$, $u(x)_i=x_i$ for $i\ne j$. Then $e\in T$, $u:T\to T$ is monotone, and both $\operatorname{id}_T\leq u$ and $c_e\leq u$ hold, where $c_e$ is the constant map at $e$. Write $h(f,g)$ for the explicit degree-raising prism maps of [lem-sfb-poset-augmented-chain-prism]. Define $R$-linear maps $t_n:C_n(T;R)\to C_{n+1}(T;R)$ by $t_n=h_n(c_e,u)-h_n(\operatorname{id}_T,u)$ for $n\geq0$, by $t_{-1}[\varnothing]=[e]$, and by zero for $n<-1$. These maps satisfy $d_{n+1}t_n+t_{n-1}d_n=\operatorname{id}_{C_n(T;R)}$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$.

proof.text: The poset $T$ is finite, being a subset of the finite product of the sets $\{0,\ldots,m_i\}$. The vector $e$ belongs to this product, is nonzero, and differs from $m$ in coordinate $j$ since $1<m_j$. For $x\in T$, every coordinate of $u(x)$ is within its bound, and $u(x)_j\geq1$, so $u(x)\ne0$. If $u(x)=m$, then $\max(x_j,1)=m_j\geq2$ forces $x_j=m_j$, while all other coordinates already equal those of $m$; this contradicts $x\ne m$. Thus $u$ maps $T$ to itself. Coordinatewise monotonicity of maximum proves monotonicity of $u$, and $x\leq u(x)$ and $e\leq u(x)$ hold coordinatewise. The identity and constant maps are monotone as well.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-poset-augmented-chain-prism] to $P=Q=T$, first to $(c_e,u)$ and then to $(\operatorname{id}_T,u)$; step 1 checks finiteness and both comparisons. Subtract the supplied identities. Writing $s=h(c_e,u)-h(\operatorname{id}_T,u)$ gives $ds+sd=(u_*-(c_e)_*)-(u_*-\operatorname{id}_*)=\operatorname{id}-(c_e)_*$ in every degree; here the identity-map clause identifies $\operatorname{id}_*$ with the identity. The prism maps are $R$-linear and $s_{-1}=0$. The displayed $t_n$ are therefore $R$-linear too, including the basis assignment in degree $-1$.

proof.text: For $n\geq1$, the constant-map formula in [lem-sfb-poset-augmented-chain-prism] sends each strict $n$-chain to the repeated tuple $[e,\ldots,e]=0$. Hence $(c_e)_{*,n}=0$. Since $t_n=s_n$ and $t_{n-1}=s_{n-1}$ for these degrees, step 2 gives $d_{n+1}t_n+t_{n-1}d_n=\operatorname{id}$.

proof.text: In degree zero, [def-sfb-augmented-poset-chains] gives $d_0[x]=[\varnothing]$, so $t_{-1}d_0[x]=[e]=(c_e)_{*,0}[x]$ by the constant-map formula of [lem-sfb-poset-augmented-chain-prism]. Step 2, with $s_{-1}=0$ and $t_0=s_0$, gives $d_1t_0=\operatorname{id}-(c_e)_{*,0}$; adding the preceding equality proves degree zero. In degree $-1$, $d_0t_{-1}[\varnothing]=d_0[e]=[\varnothing]$ and $t_{-2}d_{-1}=0$. For $n<-1$ the source module is zero. The basis calculations extend linearly, proving the identity in all integer degrees.
